claims.claim: The paper reports that model accuracy on historical facts falls as the period tested approaches the present day.
claims.source: Hauser et al., 'HiST-LLM', NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks Track (Dec 2024)
claims.quote: declines as the time frame approaches the present day

claims.claim: Across the four headline models the benchmark's worst regional performance falls on Oceania or Sub-Saharan Africa, which the authors read as a training-data bias.
claims.source: Hauser et al., 'HiST-LLM', NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks Track (Dec 2024)
claims.quote: Worst performance Oceania Oceania Oceania Sub-Sah. Africa

claims.claim: The authors caution that their first benchmark result should be read as a lower bound on model historical-knowledge performance.
claims.source: Hauser et al., 'HiST-LLM', NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks Track (Dec 2024)
claims.quote: this first benchmark should be taken as a lower bound

claims.claim: Del Rio-Chanona attributes the models' weakness to their extrapolating from prominent historical data rather than retrieving obscure knowledge.
claims.source: Kyle Wiggers, TechCrunch, reporting and quoting co-author Maria del Rio-Chanona (19 January 2025)
claims.quote: LLMs tend to extrapolate from historical data that is very prominent
claims.page: body, paragraph beginning 'Why are LLMs bad'

claims.claim: Del Rio-Chanona illustrates the mechanism as a model recalling frequently seen items and extrapolating when asked about a rarely seen one.
claims.source: Kyle Wiggers, TechCrunch, quoting Maria del Rio-Chanona (19 January 2025)
claims.quote: get told A and B 100 times, and C 1 time

claims.claim: Del Rio-Chanona says the models are good for basic facts but not for nuanced PhD-level historical inquiry.
claims.source: Maria del Rio-Chanona, quoted by Kyle Wiggers, TechCrunch (19 January 2025)

claims.claim: Turchin says the benchmark shows machine intelligence is domain-specific, strong in some contexts and very poor in others compared with humans.
claims.source: Peter Turchin, quoted in Complexity Science Hub press release (21 January 2025)

claims.claim: Del Rio-Chanona says she expected the chatbots to perform considerably better than the benchmark showed.
claims.source: R. Maria del Rio-Chanona, quoted in Complexity Science Hub press release (21 January 2025)
claims.quote: I thought the AI chatbots would do a lot better

claims.claim: On the coherency and consistency criterion the AI summaries scored 10 against the human summaries' 12, the narrowest margin of the five criteria.
claims.source: AWS Professional Services draft report attached to ASIC's answer to Question on Notice No. 001 (21 May 2024)
claims.page: Table 4, ASIC Scoring Summary by Assessment Criteria

claims.claim: ASIC chair Joe Longo told the Senate committee the AI summary of the submissions was bland rather than misleading.
claims.source: Joe Longo, ASIC Chair, Hansard extract of 21 May 2024 reproduced in ASIC's answer to Question on Notice No. 001
claims.quote: It wasn't misleading but it was bland.

claims.claim: ASIC's Greg Jefferson told the committee the AI-generated summaries were quite generic.
claims.source: Greg Jefferson, ASIC, Hansard extract of 21 May 2024 reproduced in ASIC's answer to Question on Notice No. 001

claims.claim: An ASIC assessor recorded that the model made strange choices about what to highlight in a summary.
claims.source: Unnamed ASIC assessor, rubric comment quoted in the AWS draft report attached to ASIC's answer to Question on Notice No. 001
claims.quote: Made strange choices about what to highlight.

claims.claim: An ASIC assessor described one AI summary's handling of references as wordy and pointless.
claims.source: Unnamed ASIC assessor, rubric comment quoted in the AWS draft report attached to ASIC's answer to Question on Notice No. 001

claims.claim: The AWS report lists waffliness and wordiness among the recurring themes assessors recorded about the AI summaries.
claims.source: AWS Professional Services draft report attached to ASIC's answer to Question on Notice No. 001

claims.claim: An ASIC assessor described an AI summary as dense and repetitive.
claims.source: Unnamed ASIC assessor, rubric comment quoted in Appendix C of the AWS draft report attached to ASIC's answer to Question on Notice No. 001
